sections.content:
You know *siempre que*, *con tal de que* and *a condición de que* from B2 Units 7 to 9, and *siempre y cuando* from B2 Unit 11. They say that the main clause is true only if a condition is met, and the verb after them is in the subjunctive: the present subjunctive after a present or future verb, the imperfect subjunctive after a past or conditional verb.

New here is *solo si* ("only if"). It is *si* with *solo* in front, so it follows the rules of *si* from B1 Unit 8 and B1 Unit 4: the present indicative for a real or likely condition, and the imperfect subjunctive with the conditional for an unlikely one. It never takes the present subjunctive.

sections.title: Two ways to set a strict condition
rows: Te presto el carro siempre y cuando lo devuelvas antes de las seis.
I will lend you the car provided that you give it back before six.
Te presto el carro solo si lo devuelves antes de las seis.
I will lend you the car only if you give it back before six.
Dijeron que firmarían siempre y cuando les diéramos más tiempo.
They said they would sign provided that we gave them more time.
Solo si me pagaran bien, aceptaría el trabajo.
Only if they paid me well would I accept the job.

sections.content: Choose by mood: *siempre y cuando lo devuelvas* (subjunctive) but *solo si lo devuelves* (indicative). Both mean the same thing here. *Siempre y cuando lo devuelves* and *solo si lo devuelvas* are mistakes.
